_doc: Genes that have not been shown to fire in any committed screen, and why.
The shape is `tools/inert_waivers.json`'s: a flat {tag: reason} map. Unlike
that file the reason is ENFORCED -- `tools/gene_fires.py` fails a waiver
shorter than 40 characters -- and a waiver goes STALE, failing the same
`--max 0` ratchet, the moment its gene is proven by a committed screen row
or leaves the gene tables. The list can only shrink.
Almost every entry here is grandfathered: it was in the tables before a new
gene had to show it fires. A gene added AFTER 2026-08-23 should not appear
here at all -- #2330 wrote rows for eighteen behaviours, the gate refused
four of them on their own probes, and those four were removed from the
To clear an entry: run a single-gene probe, which holds every other gene at
the baseline so any divergence is this gene alone, and commit the analysis --
-- then DELETE the entry here, or the stale-waiver check fails.

waivers.board-ignores-the-faith-war: An opt-in gene that only acts while our own faith war is running beside a board-gated Conquest declaration (live 054450Z held a 6-12x war 49 turns this way). The host's headroom guard had parked every screen at ship time, so the single-gene fires probe was deferred. Clear with a docs/gene_screens/fires/<tag>.json probe.
waivers.defence-holds-under-fire: An opt-in gene that only stops the general production pass from displacing a threatened city's walls or defender with a civilian build. The host's headroom guard had parked every screen at ship time, so the single-gene fires probe was deferred. Clear with a docs/gene_screens/fires/<tag>.json probe.
waivers.domination-targets-land-first: An opt-in gene for Domination-target seats on water maps: it only reorders the frontier, capital and hand-over picks when a rival is unreachable by land. The host's headroom guard had parked every screen at ship time, so the single-gene fires probe was deferred. Clear with a docs/gene_screens/fires/<tag>.json probe.
waivers.early-route-feeds-production: An opt-in gene that only re-prices Trader destinations inside the first ~100 Online turns (domestic Production over foreign Gold, for the t80 production-share gate). The host's headroom guard had parked every screen at ship time, so the single-gene fires probe was deferred. Clear with a docs/gene_screens/fires/<tag>.json probe.
waivers.food-focus-grows-the-small-city: Native-seat-only: the gene widens civvis_orders' city-focus request (src/bin/civvis_orders/citizen_growth.rs) and the simulator issues no city-focus orders, so no simulator screen can make it fire. Judge it on the live Immortal lane: Food surplus of small cities, citizens at t40/t60/t80 and the t80 Production share against the leader.
waivers.hidden-border-yields-to-our-pressure: Native-seat-only: the gene relaxes frontier-loyalty's unresolved-border arm, which reads Game::unseen_major_borders, a set only the live Civ VI mirror fills (fogged major borders); native games leave it empty, so no simulator screen can make it fire. Judge it on the live Immortal lane: Settler walk turns, Stranded Settler lines, cities at t60/t80, and any city lost to Loyalty.
waivers.faith-war-at-match-point: Opt-in, rides faith-war-before-the-flip-2 (off at the ledger baseline, armed on the live seat), and acts only for a seat that founded no religion when a rival founder's faith already holds every other living major and a city of ours leans to it: the last turns before a Religious defeat, which a six-game probe at the baseline does not reach. This host's compilers are parked by the CPU guard during the live game, so no screen was run. The unit tests in src/ai/advanced/faith_war_at_match_point/tests.rs pin both arms (opened at a quarter of the founder's power and past a threatened city only under the gene; no reading without the last other major or a leaning city; never on a declared friend; a denouncement when the host refuses the war; the counter-floor line not written at match point; the war kept while the match point holds). Clear with the first armed game's 'faith-war-at-match-point:' why.log lines or a captured_native_action_pairs_v1 artifact.
waivers.hint-runs-the-claims: Live-bridge only: the gene changes AdvancedAi::preview_live_production, which only civvis_orders' deferred produce_next hint calls when a Civilization VI city's item finishes after the board was exported. The native gene_screen board never issues that hint (every empty queue already runs the claim chain in take_turn_inner), so it genuinely cannot fire in the regime the screen plays. Its evidence is the live per-game on/off screen (~/.civvis-live-screen-gene) and captured-input civvis_orders --resumed replays; the unit tests pin that the hint then equals the main path's claim choice.
waivers.launch-pad-holds-its-queue: An opt-in queue hold for the empire's first unfinished Spaceport: it only changes a late-game city that placed a pad and lent its queue to a claim, a state a single-gene fires probe rarely reaches. Clear with a docs/gene_screens/fires/<tag>.json probe.
waivers.launcher-war-fights-the-faster-racer: An opt-in tie-break inside launcher-war-serves-every-lane: it only changes which racer is the counter when two space racers have the same projects landed and both pass the launcher war's gates, a late-game state a single-gene fires probe rarely reaches. Clear with a docs/gene_screens/fires/<tag>.json probe.
waivers.religion-lane-hands-over: An opt-in gene for Religion-target seats, which the live Civ VI lane only began rolling on 2026-10-31: a seat whose Prophet race is lost (every religion slot claimed, none ours) retargets to Science. It fires only after the race closes on a Religion-target seat, and the host's headroom guard had parked every screen at ship time, so the single-gene fires probe was deferred. Clear with a docs/gene_screens/fires/<tag>.json probe.
waivers.religion-lane-spreads-from-founding: An opt-in gene for Religion-target seats, which the live Civ VI lane only began rolling on 2026-10-31: it keeps a founded Religion seat's spreading posture, Faith reserve and idle-queue Shrine/Temple production while its plan reads Expansion. The host's headroom guard had parked every screen (load 90+) at ship time, so the single-gene fires probe was deferred. Clear with a docs/gene_screens/fires/<tag>.json probe.
waivers.religion-race-keeps-expanding: An opt-in gene for Religion-target seats without a religion: it only lets the existing Expansion branch answer first while the seat is short of its cities. The host's headroom guard had parked every screen at ship time, so the single-gene fires probe was deferred. Clear with a docs/gene_screens/fires/<tag>.json probe.
waivers.saved-work-is-seen: Cannot fire on a native board: Game::host_saved_work is filled only by the live mirror from the host menu's per-item `pr` (BuildQueue:GetUnitProgress/GetBuildingProgress/GetProjectProgress), and a native game has no host menu, so the gene is bit-identical there (the native engine already banks switched work in City::production_progress). Judge it live: 'resumes' journal lines per game and the share of city production stranded in builds switched away and never finished (4.9-7.9% across 38 Emperor/Immortal games on 2026-11-02).
waivers.science-drive-answers-from-the-pad: An opt-in widening of science-drive-answers-the-launch: it only changes a seat assigned another lane once a rival has landed a space project and our own landed projects are level with the leading racer's, a late-game state a single-gene fires probe rarely reaches. Clear with a docs/gene_screens/fires/<tag>.json probe.
waivers.science-drive-answers-from-the-pad-2: An opt-in widening of science-drive-answers-the-launch: it only changes a seat assigned another lane once a rival has landed a space project and our own landed projects are within one of the leading racer's, a late-game state a single-gene fires probe rarely reaches. Clear with a docs/gene_screens/fires/<tag>.json probe.
waivers.science-drive-leads-beside-the-lane: An opt-in widening of science-drive-answers-the-launch: it only changes a seat assigned another lane that leads the field outright from Online turn 140, a late-game state a single-gene fires probe rarely reaches. Clear with a docs/gene_screens/fires/<tag>.json probe.
waivers.policy-swap-keeps-the-army-paid: Opt-in policy-pass guard: it keeps a card (upkeep relief or priced Gold) whose loss would take income, projected against the deck the turn began with, to zero or below, and wants back the paying cards the base deck review gave up while that projection is at or below zero. It is expected to fire in native games, but no screen was run from this worktree: this host's compilers are parked by the CPU guard during the live game and the coordinating session's sims hold the cores. Five unit tests in src/ai/advanced/policy_swap_keeps_the_army_paid/tests.rs pin both arms. The coordinating session replaces this waiver with a fires probe from its sim worktree; the first armed game's 'policy-swap-keeps-the-army-paid:' why.log lines also clear it.
waivers.stalled-spreader-braves-the-march: An opt-in gene for Religion-target seats only: it changes the apostle evasion only for a spreader held three consecutive turns, which the native screens' seats rarely produce. The host's headroom guard had parked every screen at ship time, so the single-gene fires probe was deferred. Clear with a docs/gene_screens/fires/<tag>.json probe.
waivers.surprise-watch-holds-its-ratio: An opt-in early-defence gene for the live Civ VI seat: it latches the capital and frontier walls when a 2x major is seen within ten tiles, and only fires on rushed openings that the screen's rivals rarely produce. The host was saturated (load 90+) at ship time, so the single-gene fires probe was deferred. Clear with a docs/gene_screens/fires/<tag>.json probe.
waivers.founding-voyage: Cannot fire in the native screen: it acts only for a seat with no city whose Settler stands embarked under live fog (the Maori start, with a mirror that carries only revealed plots). Native boards reveal the whole map and seat no civilization at sea; verified instead by replaying live 20261103T142545Z with civvis-orders --mirror --turn 2 (no order without the gene, MOVE_TO with it).
waivers.ranged-finish-on-the-mean: Cannot fire in the native screen: the live finishing volley (src/ai/finishing.rs, begin_player_turn) runs only in the Civ VI decider civvis_orders via ai::player::plan_frame; native gene_screen seats never call it, so a single-gene probe reads identical arms. Exercised instead by an exact decider replay of live run civvis-20261104T012627Z (902 captured requests, base vs --with ranged-finish-on-the-mean): 4 replies differ, finishing lines 31 -> 33, finishing attacks 37 -> 39.
waivers.generals-lead-the-army: Cannot fire in the native screen: it acts only in the live bridge (src/bin/civvis_orders.rs great_person_orders_led), which walks Great Generals and Comandante Generals to a front instead of retiring them. The engine has no Great General board piece (advanced/engine_pricing.rs), so native gene_screen seats never see one and a single-gene probe reads identical arms. Exercised by the bridge unit tests in civvis_orders/generals_lead_the_army.rs; judged live by the kill/loss ratio inside the aura.
waivers.slots-survive-the-roll: A modifier of battle-planner-2 (opt-in, off in the deployment genome): it changes only the positions plan's slot_cost and position_end_tile, which run only when battle-planner-2 plays, so a single-gene probe with the family off reads identical arms. Pinned by battle_planner::roll_tests (a slot between the centre blow and the top of its roll is refused; a unit short of its slot ends on the nearest tile the roll does not remove it on); measured as a paired read on the live genome, where battle-planner-2 is armed.
waivers.camps-close-the-age: An opt-in Objective Board modifier that reads only when objective-board plays (off in the deployment genome; armed live) and a seat stands one to six Era Score short of its Normal Age while a destroyed camp still scores, so a single-gene probe with the board off reads identical arms. Pinned by objective_board::camp_age_tests; measured as a paired read on the live genome, where objective-board is armed.
waivers.camps-close-the-age-2: Version two of camps-close-the-age, the same Objective Board modifier: it reads only while objective-board plays (off in the deployment genome; armed live) and a seat stands one to six Era Score short of its Normal Age while a destroyed camp still scores, so a single-gene probe with the board off reads identical arms. Pinned by objective_board::camp_age_tests; measured as a paired read on the live genome.
waivers.capital-keeps-its-defender: An opt-in Objective Board reordering that reads only while objective-board plays (off in the deployment genome; armed live) and our capital has a Defend row, which the native screen's rival chairs rarely force: they befriend the measured seat and almost never declare (see #4429). Pinned by objective_board::capital_defender_tests; measured with defence_replay on the live capital losses and a paired read under --rival-war-pace.
waivers.camps-close-the-age-3: Version three of camps-close-the-age, the same Objective Board modifier: it reads only while objective-board plays (off in the deployment genome; armed live) and a barbarian camp stands within CAMP_NEAR_RADIUS of our cities (or the seat is closing an Age), so a single-gene probe with the board off reads identical arms. Pinned by objective_board::camp_age_tests; measured as a paired read on the live genome.
waivers.denial-spies-skip-the-upkeep-wait: Opt-in waiver of upkeep-waits-for-the-income for a Spy the space denial still wants (live Deity Gran Colombia lane). It acts only on a Domination seat past the upkeep gate's first turn (live t120), with science-denial-trains-spies on, a rival past its Moon and short of its launch, the gate holding a Spy, and a treasury that carries that Spy's own upkeep for 15 turns; upkeep-waits-for-the-income and science-denial-trains-spies are opt-in and off at the ledger baseline (armed on the live seat), so a single-gene probe at the baseline never reaches it. This host's compilers are parked by the CPU guard during the live game, so no screen was run. The unit tests in src/ai/advanced/denial_spies_skip_the_upkeep_wait/tests.rs pin both arms (the claimed Spy is set aside by the stock gate and keeps its queue under the gene, with a journal line naming the racer; a tank still waits; the Earth Satellite alone, a launched Expedition, a treasury short of the Spy's own runway, a denial already supplied and the claim off all keep the wait). Clear with the first armed game's 'denial-spies-skip-the-upkeep-wait:' why.log lines or a captured_native_action_pairs_v1 artifact.
waivers.capital-keeps-its-defender-2: Version two of capital-keeps-its-defender, an Objective Board reordering that reads only while objective-board plays (off in the deployment genome; armed live) and one of our first three cities has a Defend row or a hostile in relief range, which the native screen's rival chairs rarely force (see #4429). Pinned by objective_board::capital_defender_tests; measured under --rival-war-pace and live by early-city losses.
waivers.capital-keeps-its-defender-3: Version three of capital-keeps-its-defender, an Objective Board reordering that reads only while objective-board plays (off in the deployment genome; armed live) and a stronger major's soldier stands within SURPRISE_TILES of one of our first three cities, which the native screen's befriending rival chairs rarely produce (see #4429). Pinned by objective_board::capital_defender_tests; measured under --rival-war-pace and live by early-city losses.
waivers.centre-keeps-its-garrison: Opt-in. Acts only at war while a visible enemy land soldier stands within three tiles of one of our cities (the garrison keeps the City Center, or an empty centre takes a soldier in reach); the native screen's befriending rival chairs rarely declare on the measured seat (see #4429), and this host's compilers are parked by the CPU guard during the live game, so no screen was run. The unit tests in src/ai/advanced/centre_keeps_its_garrison/tests.rs pin both arms (off reads nothing and leaves the board; a shooter keeper fires from the centre and stays; a melee keeper holds through a whole turn; an empty centre takes a soldier in reach; no threat, peace, a Scout, a centre out of reach or already held take nothing), and paired_posed_defences plays 96 posed two-city defences ten turns with the gene off and on, on CI (cities lost 80 -> 75, empty threatened centres at turn end 257 -> 169). Clear with a paired gene_screen under --rival-war-pace or the first armed game's 'centre-keeps-its-garrison:' why.log lines.
waivers.walls-release-the-one-blow: A modifier of defenders-hold-the-walls (armed live; off in the deployment genome): it changes only which units holds_the_walls keeps, while a hostile at war stands within two tiles of one of our cities and a ring defender's own tile is one-blow lethal, which the native screen's befriending rival chairs rarely produce (see #4429). Pinned by defenders_hold_the_walls::tests; measured under --rival-war-pace and live by late-war unit losses.
waivers.threatened-lane-lends-the-army: An opt-in gene that only lends a non-Domination seat's delegated governor the war army target while at war with a major and a home city is threatened (live Deity 033244Z t168: 8 military for 6 cities against a target of 1.0 each, in Recovery at 577 power against 3377). The host's headroom guard parked every civvis build at ship time (load 50-110), so the paired native-query fires proof on 033244Z t168 was deferred. Clear with docs/gene_screens/fires/<tag>.action-pairs.json.
waivers.anvil-spares-the-one-blow: A modifier of the Anvil (armed live; off in the deployment genome): it rewrites posts only while an Anvil defends a threatened city under fire, which the native screen's rarely-warring rival chairs seldom produce (see #4429); measured with the calibrated war-pace field. Pinned by anvil_spares_the_one_blow::tests (the city tile is never left to nobody; a post one blow removes its soldier on is moved).
waivers.ranged-kills-are-free: A modifier of the battle planner's kill search (battle-planner-2 armed live; off in the deployment genome): it changes candidates only for a recovering, guarding or doomed ranged shooter with a blow from its own tile, a state the native screen's rarely-warring rival chairs seldom produce (see #4429). Pinned by battle_planner::tests (kill-only shots join a sequence that kills and nothing less); verified by an exact decider replay of live 20261105T044106Z.
waivers.settler-shelters-from-the-war-2: Version two of settler-shelters-from-the-war: the same wartime shelter, without version one's peace clause (which held the second Settler up to ten turns in the opening of 3 of the first 5 live carriers). Its wartime behaviour is version one's, proven by docs/gene_screens/fires/settler-shelters-from-the-war.action-pairs.json (044106Z t98, at war); the version-two paired query was deferred while the headroom guard parked every build. Clear with docs/gene_screens/fires/<tag>.action-pairs.json.
waivers.capture-scar-reads-the-new-city: Deferred: the gene changes how the live capture lessons resolve a Settler that left the board between two turns, so its effect needs the previous turn's settler_last_seen and city record, which a one-turn --resumed native query starts without. Unit test civilian_safety::tests::a_settler_taken_beside_a_standing_city_scars_the_ground_under_the_gene covers both arms. Live motivation: 173830Z t96 (taken one tile from its city, no scar) then t102 (taken three tiles from that spot). Clear with docs/gene_screens/fires/<tag>.action-pairs.json from a two-turn live replay, or a live journal line 'vanished beside a standing city'.
waivers.group-steps-read-the-field: A modifier of the group step's danger memory (unit-objective-memory, deployment genome): it raises the approach reading only where the danger field sees a hostile the one-step forecast does not, a state the native screen's rarely-warring rival chairs seldom produce (see #4429); measured with the calibrated war-pace field and live. Pinned by group_steps_read_the_field::tests (a fast hostile the one-step forecast misses is read by the field).
waivers.band-buys-near-the-stage: Changes only which of our cities a Culture seat's Rock Band purchase tries first: the city nearest a stage (our bands' host concert highlights, else seen wonders and Theater Squares of open rivals). The standard fires probe buys few Rock Bands, and with one city near the stage the buy is identical, so a single-gene probe reads identical arms. Three unit tests in advanced/band_buys_near_the_stage.rs pin the order; the motivating live games are the 14 culture games of 2026-11-10 that bought bands (median 9 hexes from the buying city to the nearest highlighted stage, 4 from the nearest city; 41 of 125 bands never played). Captured action pairs from the first armed Culture game with two or more cities replace this waiver.
waivers.government-reach-pays-the-switch: Deferred: the gene acts on a live Science seat holding Communism with Corporate Libertarianism unlocked, reached only late in the seats closest to a win, so a short native screen rarely gets there; a captured action pair on civvis-20261105T111305Z t187 is planned before any arm request. Unit test a_two_slot_gain_does_not_pay_for_the_switch covers both arms.
waivers.world-religion-condemns-the-faith: Deferred: the gene acts only while World Religion option B is in force, and option B passed in none of the 74 recorded sessions (11-01 to 11-05), so no captured frame can show a changed order until the ballot half lands. Unit tests world_religion_condemns::tests cover both arms on the board; tools/civ6_control/mod/world_religion_condemn_test.lua covers the ballot.
waivers.science-seat-races-the-congress: Live-only ballot change: the agent's CivvisCongressRacer casts it on the native World Congress, which the simulator does not model and which the Rust decider never reads (the field is set only so --with reaches tools/civ6_play.py). No simulator probe or native action pair can fire it. Pinned instead by racer_ballot_test.lua and public_works_vote_test.lua; clear only if the sim gains the Congress.
waivers.field-reads-the-tile-it-leaves: A modifier of the battle planner's danger field (strike-reach is in the deployment genome): it adds a blow only where a hostile that can strike a unit's own tile could hit the tile it moves to, a state the native screen's rarely-warring rival chairs seldom produce (see #4429); verified by an exact decider replay of live 045954Z t87. Pinned by battle_planner::tests (the field reads a hostile stepping into the tile the unit leaves).
waivers.science-seat-builds-the-statue: Opt-in companion to the live-only Congress hedge: it needs a Science seat at t120+ with diplo-seat-wonder-claim and diplo-seat-statue-harbor armed and Civil Engineering in hand, and its value is Diplomatic Victory Points, which the simulator's Congress does not score. Pinned by the diplo_statue_harbor and diplo_wonder_claim tests; judged on the live randomized screen. Clear with a native action pair from a carrier.
waivers.religion-seat-builds-holy-sites: Gated to a founder whose target is Religion, which the standard fires probe does not seat. PR #4795 reads it in paired Deity Khmer arms on `--target-mix religion`: Faith per turn moves with it on. A committed targeted probe replaces this waiver.
waivers.religion-seat-fields-apostles: Gated to a Religion-target founder on the offensive with a Temple standing, which the standard fires probe does not seat. PR #4795 reads it in paired Deity Khmer arms on `--target-mix religion`. A committed targeted probe replaces this waiver.
waivers.religion-seat-presses-the-campaign: Gated to a Religion-target founder with rival Apostles in reach, which the standard fires probe does not seat. PR #4795 reads it in paired Deity Khmer arms on `--target-mix religion`. A committed targeted probe replaces this waiver.
waivers.religion-seat-flips-the-cheapest: Gated to a Religion-target founder choosing among foreign targets, which the standard fires probe does not seat. It reorders targets rather than adding an action, so proof needs a paired `--target-mix religion` probe, which replaces this waiver.
waivers.religion-seat-reaches-reformed-church: Gated to a Religion-target founder with Theology, which the standard fires probe does not seat. It sets one civic goal, and a paired `--target-mix religion` probe of the combined Religion genes replaces this waiver.
waivers.religion-seat-races-the-prophet: Gated to a Religion-target seat that has not founded, which the standard fires probe does not seat. Its effect is on when the Prophet arrives in live Deity games, where the Prophet class closes at a median t39. A targeted probe or live read replaces this waiver.
waivers.religion-seat-takes-the-faith-beliefs: Gated to the founding of a Religion-target seat, which the standard fires probe does not seat, and it changes one choice at founding. PR #4795 carries it in the combined paired Deity Khmer arm. A committed targeted probe replaces this waiver.
waivers.battle-solver: Fires only with a land fight in reach, which the standard fires probe seats rarely and at low power. Its effect is measured where fights happen: battle_bench 300 seeds per army against the live tactical stack, diverging on every seed, and doctrine_arena fires 24/24 on all 13 positions.
waivers.solver-plays-the-host: Opt-in; acts only inside the battle solver's rollouts (it replaces the modelled enemy's strike, target and advance with tables fitted to the live host), and battle-solver is opt-in and off at the ledger baseline, so a single-gene probe at the baseline reads identical arms. This host's compilers are parked by the CPU guard during the live game, so no screen was run. The unit tests in src/ai/advanced/battle_solver/host_enemy.rs pin both arms (the enemy strikes at the fitted rate rather than half the time, takes the unit beside it rather than the greedy trade, and closes at the fitted rate with nothing in reach), and host_enemy_bench plays battle_bench and doctrine_arena with it on against off. Clear with a paired battle_bench row or a gene_screen with battle-solver held on.
waivers.gold-unit-buys-read-the-host-quote: Opt-in; changes only BasicAi::buy_gold_unit, the Builder, Trader and Settler Gold buys of spend_gold, which then test each city's own quote (Game::unit_purchase_cost) against the reserve instead of the list price cost * 4. It is expected to fire natively wherever the engine's quote and the list price disagree, but no screen was run from this worktree: this host's compilers are parked by the CPU guard during the live game and the coordinating session's sims hold the cores. Four unit tests in src/ai/gold_spending_quote_tests.rs pin both arms (the live t192 Builder quoted 400 against a 200 list price is bought off and refused on; a quote inside the reserve is bought in both; a quote under the list price is bought only on; each city is tested on its own quote). The coordinating session replaces this waiver with a fires probe.
waivers.russia-settles-the-tundra: Gated to a Russian seat, which the standard fires probe does not seat, and data/civs.json models Mother Russia as a flat per-city bonus so a headless read cannot show the tile yields it prices. PR #4840 records a paired replay of live Deity Russia civvis-20261109T142418Z where t70 changes the next build from a Monument to a Settler. A committed targeted probe replaces this waiver.
waivers.religion-seat-first-shrine: Gated to a Religion-target seat that has founded and owns no Shrine, which the standard fires probe does not seat. Six unit tests pin the claim. PR #4844 records paired replays of live Deity Russia civvis-20261109T142418Z where 5 of 7 turns gain a produce BUILDING_SHRINE order. A committed targeted probe replaces this waiver.
waivers.religion-seat-guards-the-race: Gated to a Religion-target seat with a pillaged Holy Site or a Prayers project finishing as it is displaced, which the standard fires probe does not seat. Its six unit tests pin both branches. Live Deity Russia civvis-20261109T141812Z is the motivating game. A committed targeted probe replaces this waiver.
waivers.band-bank-bars-people-under-fire: Changes a Culture seat's Faith spending only between Ideology (or Nationalism) and Cold War, on a turn one of its cities was attacked in the last four turns, when the Great Person pass would buy out a race with the Rock Band bank. The standard fires probe rarely puts a Culture seat under fire inside that window with the Faith to patronize, so a single-gene probe reads identical arms. A unit test in advanced/culture_band_bank.rs pins both arms; the motivating live game is civvis-20261110T232642Z (1,990 Faith on a Writer at t123, one turn before Cold War, while Mycenae was under fire). Captured action pairs from the first armed Culture game with such a turn replace this waiver.
waivers.apostle-evangelizes-unspent: Gated to an Apostle below its ruleset charge count with a belief slot open, which the standard fires probe does not seat. Five unit tests pin the rule. The live evidence is 82 of 82 refusals at 2 charges against 17 of 17 landings at 3 or more across the 2026-11-09 Russia Deity games. A committed targeted probe replaces this waiver.
waivers.bands-draw-from-the-bar: Changes a Rock Band's tour only where the host offers concert plots in two or more rivals' land and a rival other than the bar holder would win under band-plays-its-stage's 1 + D/bar. The only captured live runs with our own bands (civvis-20261109T190910Z and civvis-20261110T120557Z, 16 paired decider queries at t186-207) never present that: 190910Z's band already toured the bar holder, Inca, with one rival above every other host, where the two factors agree; 120557Z's bands were offered Canada's plots alone. Six unit tests pin the factor and the tour. Captured action pairs from the first armed Culture game with bands replace this waiver.
waivers.band-plays-what-it-can-reach: Changes a Rock Band's move only when the host walked one of its trips nowhere (the band still stands where it set out the turn before), when the step toward its best venue is refused on the board itself, or when a promotion's stages lie behind Music Censorship or beyond fifteen turns. A native board never refuses a step it planned, and the standard fires probe seats few Rock Bands, so a single-gene probe reads identical arms. The motivating live game is civvis-20261110T164254Z (65 of 102 band-turns idle at a closed border); four unit tests in advanced/band_plays_what_it_can_reach.rs pin both arms. Captured action pairs from the first armed Culture game with bands replace this waiver.
waivers.bands-wait-at-the-door: Changes a Rock Band's move only on a turn it has no stage it can play or walk to while a rival at peace bars our bands from land holding a stage we have seen (Music Censorship natively; on a live board the host's concert highlights, mirror::band_closed_hosts). The standard fires probe seats few Rock Bands and its rivals rarely slot Music Censorship, so a single-gene probe reads identical arms. Three unit tests in advanced/bands_wait_at_the_door.rs pin both arms; the motivating live games are civvis-20261110T192354Z and civvis-20261110T164254Z. Captured action pairs from the first armed Culture game with a closed rival replace this waiver.
waivers.band-plays-at-level-three: Changes a Rock Band's move only for a band below performance level 3 with a stage it would play at level 3 or more within four turns that the scorer does not already rank first, and its promotion only when an offered promotion lifts an open, reachable stage. The standard fires probe seats few Rock Bands, so a single-gene probe reads identical arms. Two unit tests in advanced/band_plays_at_level_three.rs pin both arms; the motivating live games are civvis-20261110T205256Z (eight of nine bands broke up within two concerts) and civvis-20261110T173750Z. Captured action pairs from the first armed Culture game with bands replace this waiver.
waivers.band-stage-needs-three-venues: Changes a Rock Band's promotion only under band-plays-at-level-three, when an offered two-level promotion (Glam, Arena or Reggae Rock) has one or two counted stages and the band would otherwise take it for reaching level 3. The standard fires probe seats few Rock Bands and rarely offers that choice, so a single-gene probe reads identical arms. A unit test in advanced/band_plays_its_stage.rs pins both arms; the motivating live choices are ten first promotions of 2026-11-10 that took Arena or Reggae Rock over Album Cover Art, Space, Surf or Glam Rock (Reggae over Glam in civvis-20261110T192354Z). Captured action pairs from the first armed Culture game with such an offer replace this waiver.
waivers.band-stall-bars-no-host: Changes a Rock Band's tour only on a turn the host walked one of its trips nowhere (the band still stands where it set out the turn before) under band-plays-what-it-can-reach: the first such turn bars no host. A native board never refuses a step it planned, and the standard fires probe seats few Rock Bands, so a single-gene probe reads identical arms. Three unit tests in advanced/band_stall_bars_no_host.rs pin both arms; the motivating live game is civvis-20261110T232642Z, where the host moved no unit of ours at t143 and all four travelling bands were barred from the Culture bar holder at t144. Captured action pairs from the first armed Culture game with a stalled turn replace this waiver.
waivers.peace-waits-for-the-host-minimum: An opt-in gene that only withholds a peace offer to a major whose war on us is younger than the host's minimum war length. It cannot change a native board: the engine refuses every peace deal inside that minimum (peace_available_at), and the report's peace offers are read only by the live bridge (civvis_orders). A one-shot civvis_orders replay starts with no record of when the war began, so captured action pairs cannot show it either. Clear with a live arm: why.log 'Holding the peace offer' lines and peace_request events at war age 8.
waivers.rear-cities-grow-through-the-war-hold: Acts only while the opt-in threatened-war-holds-the-claims holds the claims (armed on the live Deity Gran Colombia Domination seat), and only for the opt-in growth claims it reopens (granary-claims-the-bound-queue, aqueduct-claims-the-capped-queue, neighborhood-houses-the-capped-city, backlog-builder-takes-the-queue, campus-building-claims-the-queue, parallel-library-backlog, trader-fills-the-idle-route); a single-gene probe holds every other gene at the ledger baseline, where the hold and those claims are off, so its arms read identical. No screen was run: this host's compilers are parked by the CPU guard during the live game. Five unit tests in src/ai/advanced/rear_cities_grow_through_the_war_hold/tests.rs pin both arms (a pressed front city keeps the hold while the rear city claims its Granary; off, neither claims; a city hit two turns ago or named threatened is the front; the quickest rear city claims its University while the named front does not). Clear with the first armed game's 'Rear cities grow through the war hold' why.log lines or a captured_native_action_pairs_v1 artifact.
waivers.settler-stall-counts-turns: Changes only how often SETTLER_STALL_LIMIT counts: at most once per game turn, and not on a turn the Settler got closer. The bite is per decision frame (the live bridge replans 2-3 frames a turn and steps a held Settler in each), which neither a single replayed frame (civvis_orders --resumed starts a fresh agent with empty stall counters) nor a native screen (one frame a turn) can show; the native only diverges when an end-of-move stall follows progress and two held turns follow. Three unit tests in advanced/settler_stall_counts_turns.rs pin both arms (three frames of one turn count one stall and keep the site; the limit still releases after three turns and journals the drop; off, every frame counts). Motivating live game: civvis-20261111T000134Z t20. Captured live why.log lines from the first armed game (the new 'sets (X) aside after 3 stalled turns' line) replace this waiver.
waivers.tribute-warms-the-neighbour: A live-bridge-only gene: civvis_orders appends the Gold gift from the host's opinion breakdown and diplomatic state, which the native simulator does not model (STANDARD_DIPLOMATIC_ONE_SIDED_TRADES), so no screen can fire it. The bridge test neighbour_tribute_warms_the_nearest_stronger_cold_neighbour pins the order; clear with a captured_native_action_pairs_v1 artifact from a live Deity frame.
waivers.city-state-before-the-first-capital: Acts only on a seat assigned Domination with the opt-in early-conquest-opening on (the live Macedon seat arms it, and first-capital-before-the-walls beside it); a single-gene probe holds every other gene at the ledger baseline, where early-conquest-opening is off, so its arms read identical. Seventeen unit tests in advanced/city_state_before_the_first_capital/tests.rs pin the naming, the reservation, the declaration on the city-state, the plan and Siege row on its city and the capture; the paired live-genome read was deferred on 2026-11-11 while the build host was saturated, and the live seat reads it first.
waivers.faith-war-on-a-small-world: Opt-in, rides faith-war-before-the-flip-2. Not yet replayed: the paired civvis_orders query on the motivating frame (civvis-20261111T040245Z t52, Macedon Deity 4-player Pangaea, held live on power 199 against the Netherlands' steady 398 at race 50%) was dropped because the host's compilers were parked by the CPU guard during a live game (seven concurrent civvis builds), and no native screen plays a 4-major Deity Pangaea with a founder's spreaders at our cities. Nine unit tests in advanced/faith_war_before_the_flip/tests.rs pin both arms on a 4-major board (off: held on power at 0.5x; on: opened at 0.25x, 0.5x and 2x, kept at peace while the race holds; 6 majors unchanged). Clear with a captured_native_action_pairs_v1 artifact from that frame, or the first armed game's 'Opening the faith war on' line tagged faith-war-on-a-small-world.
waivers.own-flip-faith-war-asks-no-power: Opt-in, rides faith-war-on-a-small-world and faith-war-before-the-flip-2 (both off at the ledger baseline, armed on the live seat), and acts only on a world of four living majors or fewer when a founder's faith holds no other major, half our cities lean to it and our power is under half its steady power: a six-game probe at the baseline does not reach it. This host's compilers are parked by the CPU guard during the live game, so no screen was run. The unit tests in src/ai/advanced/own_flip_faith_war/tests.rs pin both arms (opened on our own flip at a quarter of the founder's power only under the gene; a threatened city and the income gate still hold it; the own-flip thresholds unchanged; a denouncement when the host refuses the war; the counter floor lifted for that founder). Clear with the first armed game's 'own-flip-faith-war-asks-no-power:' why.log lines or a captured_native_action_pairs_v1 artifact.
waivers.open-city-is-the-objective: Opt-in, Domination lane only, and acts only while the seat is at war with a major that owns a city with no walls standing and our land melee within eight tiles would take it within five turns by the combat formula (live Deity 2026-11-12: 143 war-turns in 45 games, most past turn 60): the native screen's baseline seldom fields that war and army at once, and this host's compilers are parked by the CPU guard during the live game, so no screen was run. The unit tests in src/ai/advanced/open_city_objective/tests.rs pin both arms (off: nothing is read; on: the open city outranks a walled objective, its war is a front, no peace while the capture stands, the siege goes on the train's own takers) and every hold (walls, peace, the tier floor, the march, the local check, a falling city of ours, outmatched, the one-war threat/capital/rout closures). Clear with the first armed game's 'open-city-is-the-objective:' why.log lines or a paired gene_screen.
waivers.breaker-walks-under-a-shield: Acts only on a seat with the opt-in early-conquest-opening on (the live Macedon Domination seat arms it beside first-capital-before-the-walls and city-state-before-the-first-capital), and only once that opening holds a Battering Ram or Siege Tower; a single-gene probe holds every other gene at the ledger baseline, where early-conquest-opening is off, so its arms read identical. The unit tests in advanced/breaker_walks_under_a_shield/tests.rs pin both arms (the march stacked with its shield, the hold and the strike beside the ram, walls down, the journalled loss and the shipped release, a whole-turn city-state strike with the siege train armed); the paired siege_replay on the live boards 040704Z and 072641Z ran on the CI runner (PR #5076) while this host's compilers were parked. Clear with the first armed game's 'Breaker under a shield:' lines or a captured_native_action_pairs_v1 artifact.
waivers.education-follows-the-library: Opt-in research goal for a Domination seat (live Deity Gran Colombia lane) that fires only once an owned city holds a Campus with a Library and Education is unknown; a single-gene probe at the ledger baseline rarely reaches that state before the Domination lane's own goals, and this host's compilers are parked by the CPU guard during the live game, so no screen was run. The four unit tests in src/ai/advanced/research/domination_education/tests.rs prove the decision. Clear with the first armed game's 'education-follows-the-library:' why.log lines or a captured_native_action_pairs_v1 artifact.
waivers.opening-scout-comes-back: Acts only on two rare opening events: the opening's barbarian defence taking a city's queue from a Scout (the Scout is then owed and becomes that city's next build), and a Scout lost before 37 standard turns while no major rival's original capital is charted (one replacement a game, in the capital). Live Deity Gran Colombia saw the first in 3 and the second in 1 of 24 games of 2026-11-11 (200336Z, 222533Z, 230722Z, 223549Z); a six-game single-gene probe at the ledger baseline mostly draws neither, so its arms read identical, and this host's compilers were parked by the live lane when the PR (#5152) was written. The four unit tests in src/ai/scout_first/tests.rs pin both decisions and their gates. Clear with the first armed game's 'trains the Scout the barbarian defence displaced' or 'replaces the lost Scout at once' lines, or a captured_native_action_pairs_v1 artifact.
waivers.the-worked-backlog-gets-its-builder-firs: Opt-in; acts only through builders-cover-the-worked-backlog's step and backlog-builder-takes-the-queue's claim, both opt-in and off at the ledger baseline (armed on the live Deity Gran Colombia seat), so a single-gene probe reads identical arms. This host's compilers were parked by the CPU guard during the live game when the PR was written, so no screen was run. Four unit tests in src/ai/advanced/the_worked_backlog_gets_its_builder_first/tests.rs pin both arms (a backlog past the stock 60% cover and a three-tile backlog with no charge call a Builder only under the gene, the governor holds it, one tile of slack calls none, the early claim takes one queue and keeps Settler, Trader and Walls heads, and does nothing without its carrier). Clear with the first armed game's 'the-worked-backlog-gets-its-builder-first:' why.log lines or a captured_native_action_pairs_v1 artifact.
waivers.commercial-hub-claims-a-peace-queue: Opt-in queue claim for a Domination seat (live Deity Gran Colombia lane) that rides commercial-hub-in-the-strategic-queue (armed live, off at the ledger baseline), so a single-gene probe at the baseline never opens its window; this host's compilers are parked by the CPU guard during the live game, so no screen was run. The four unit tests in src/ai/advanced/commercial_hub_claims_a_peace_queue/tests.rs prove each decision. Clear with the first armed game's 'commercial-hub-claims-a-peace-queue:' why.log lines or a captured_native_action_pairs_v1 artifact.
waivers.domination-seat-raises-its-culture: Opt-in for a Domination seat (live Deity Gran Colombia lane): a Monument claim that passes only a Granary, an Aqueduct, a soldier at peace or an idle queue in a city of two citizens or more, and a Connoisseur that acts only through domination-seat-appoints-pingala-first, which is armed live but off at the ledger baseline, so a single-gene probe at the baseline reaches only the Monument half; this host's compilers are parked by the CPU guard during the live game, so no screen was run. The unit tests in src/ai/advanced/domination_culture/tests.rs pin both arms (the Monument passes a soldier, a Granary and an Aqueduct only under the gene and only for a Domination seat; a Settler, Builder, Trader, Walls, Campus, Library, Commercial Hub, Holy Site, siege gun, an item finishing this turn, a one-citizen, threatened or attacked city and a soldier at war keep their queue; Connoisseur is the third title and Magnus the fourth, Victor first under Recovery). Clear with the first armed game's 'domination-seat-raises-its-culture:' why.log lines or a paired simulation.
waivers.first-campus-before-the-settler: Opt-in claim exception for a Domination seat (live Deity Gran Colombia lane) that rides campus-claims-the-free-slot(-2) and the early Settler floor (both armed live, off at the ledger baseline), so a single-gene probe at the baseline never reaches a floor-held first Campus; this host's compilers are parked by the CPU guard during the live game, so no screen was run. The unit tests in src/ai/advanced/first_campus_before_the_settler/tests.rs pin both arms (the first Campus goes ahead of the floor's Settler only under the gene, the Settler keeps its progress, the floor then leaves the capital's Campus alone, and war, rush, threat, one city, a slow Campus, a better site elsewhere, another victory target or an existing Campus keep the Settler). Clear with the first armed game's 'first-campus-before-the-settler:' why.log lines or a captured_native_action_pairs_v1 artifact.
waivers.campus-and-library-before-the-claims: Opt-in claim exception for a Domination seat (live Deity Gran Colombia lane) that rides campus-claims-the-free-slot(-2) and opens campus-building-claims-the-queue for the Library; its holds pass only when another claim (backlog Builder, bound Granary, capped Aqueduct, producer Industrial Zone, the deterrent) or the deferral rule holds a Campus or Library, and those claims are armed live but off at the ledger baseline, so a single-gene probe at the baseline barely reaches it; this host's compilers are parked by the CPU guard during the live game, so no screen was run. The unit tests in src/ai/advanced/campus_and_library_before_the_claims/tests.rs pin both arms (the first Campus passes a Builder and every Library passes a Commercial Hub with progress only under the gene, the displaced items keep their progress, the claim opens with campus-building-claims-the-queue off, and a Settler, Walls, a threatened or attacked city, another victory target and a soldier at war keep their queue). Clear with the first armed game's 'campus-and-library-before-the-claims:' why.log lines or a captured_native_action_pairs_v1 artifact.
waivers.hopeless-army-yields-the-queue: Opt-in for a Domination seat (live Deity Gran Colombia lane). It acts only while the plan's target city stands behind walls that nothing we field or can build would breach and take within 15 turns (or, for its deterrence half, against a neighbour fielding twice our power), and its reservation, breaker and deterrence hooks ride lane-delegates-production-2, domination-target-gets-its-breaker and near-rival-deterrence, all opt-in and off at the ledger baseline (armed on the live seat); only its scorer clamp can act at the baseline, on a Domination seat at war with such walls, which a six-game probe rarely reaches. This host's compilers are parked by the CPU guard during the live game, so no screen was run. The unit tests in src/ai/advanced/hopeless_army_yields_the_queue/tests.rs pin both arms (the reading; no gun reserved, restored or claimed for hopeless walls while a breachable target keeps its gun; the scorer prices one garrison a city unless the city is threatened or under fire; the deterrent stops at a ranged garrison and holds only a garrisonless city's). Clear with the first armed game's 'hopeless-army-yields-the-queue:' why.log lines or a captured_native_action_pairs_v1 artifact.
waivers.endgame-army-takes-the-queue: Opt-in Domination production claim (live Deity Gran Colombia lane) that opens only past 60% of the clock or within 50 turns of a rival's projected victory, on a seat whose victory target is Domination; this task's brief forbade gene_screen and sims on this host while the live game and the coordinator's sims run, so no probe was made and the coordinator sim-tests it. The unit tests in src/ai/advanced/endgame_army_takes_the_queue/tests.rs pin both arms (off or another target changes nothing; the window opens at 60% without a rival capital and on a rival space launch; idle cities train land units while the income carries them, an insolvent treasury claims nothing and a bank pays the runway, the unit bill bounds the count, a threatened or recently hit city keeps its queue, a fresh long-payback build gives its queue while Walls and a half-paid build stay, the army at its target leaves the queues alone, and the endgame reserve is three turns of the unit bill). Clear with the coordinator's paired sim or the first armed game's 'endgame-army-takes-the-queue:' why.log lines.
waivers.deterrence-stops-at-a-garrison: Opt-in, not armed: split out of hopeless-army-yields-the-queue (#5169) after the 11-12 live arm. It acts only on a Domination seat through near-rival-deterrence (opt-in, off at the ledger baseline) against a neighbour fielding twice our power or more, so a single-gene probe at the baseline reads identical arms; this host's compilers are parked by the CPU guard during the live game, so no screen was run. The unit tests in src/ai/advanced/deterrence_stops_at_a_garrison/tests.rs pin both arms (a garrisoned city trains no deterrent and a garrisonless one only an Archer, within reach the deterrent stands, the hold keeps only a garrisonless city's Archer, and the siege gene alone or another lane leaves the deterrent alone). Clear with an armed game's 'deterrence-stops-at-a-garrison:' why.log lines or a captured_native_action_pairs_v1 artifact.
